## Rule (DECODED 2026-07-03, batch48)

Input is a **6-row** grid, one-hot over 10 color channels. **Only row 0 has colored "seed" pixels**; rows 1–5 are background. Each seed at `(0, c)` with color `v` produces a vertical **diamond lattice** (period 2):
- **Even output rows (0,2,4):** `v` at column `c` (seed copied straight down).
- **Odd output rows (1,3,5):** `v` at columns `c-1` and `c+1`.

Verified: reconstructs all 265 train+test+arc-gen outputs exactly. All inputs are 6 rows tall, width ≤15, **min seed gap = 3** (gaps ∈ {3,4} only) → at most one seed per 3-col window.

**LIVE 190-graph** = a single grouped `Conv`, `kernel[10,1,6,3]` (180) + `bias[10]` (10), group=10, pads `[5,1,0,1]`. Channels 1–9 share a checkerboard 6×3 kernel (the diamond generator); channel 0 is a special background-complement kernel (rowsums all 0 except `ky5`=6 → uniform background value 6) with `bias=-5` (→ background decodes to 1). This is NOT the stale 19-node / 11,245-byte crop15col graph in the AUTO blocks below.

## Cost analysis + FLOOR PROOF (WALL @ 190, batch48 2026-07-03)

Cost model = `params (initializer element count) + memory (intermediate-tensor bytes; input/output excluded)`. LIVE single-Conv: params=190, **memory=0** (no intermediates). `profile_real_cost --arcgen 266` = 190 (static=profile=190). Bar (ng_current_bar, manifest-authoritative) = **190**, sha `d48db5f200e4…`.

**Every component is forced:**
1. Output = 10 one-hot channels, each a function of only its own input channel (color independence) ⇒ depthwise `group=10` conv, kernel `[10,1,·,·]`.
2. Filling 6 output rows from the single populated input row (row0) ⇒ vertical taps at offsets 0–5 ⇒ **kernel height 6** (can't be less).
3. Diamond needs horizontal taps at −1,0,+1 ⇒ **kernel width 3** (width 2 can't express both the even-row center tap and odd-row ±1 taps).
   ⇒ kernel = 10·6·3 = **180 params, forced**.
4. **Bias (10) is forced too.** Bottom output row 5 (odd) carves its diamond foreground *only* through kernel row `ky0` (the only row that reaches input row0 for output row 5); its ±1 taps `a₀,c₀` must be ≥ the background value T>0. But padding cell **output(row=10, col=W)** reads only input(row5, col W−1)=1, giving `conv = a₀`; it must be ≤0 (expected empty). Same weight required `>0` and `≤0` ⇒ impossible without a constant negative offset. The Conv bias is the *only* free way to inject that offset (an `Add` node would cost a `[1,10,30,30]`=36,000-byte intermediate). Bias length must = M=10 (a shorter bias is UB — traps §8h). ⇒ **bias = 10 params, forced.**
5. No 2-op reformulation helps: any second node materializes a non-`output` intermediate (smallest useful ≈ Slice row0 = 1,200 B) > the 10 params it could save. Single-Conv (0 memory) is optimal.

**Total 190 = 180 + 10, forced. This IS the floor.** The prompt's `floor_est ~110` was derived from the stale 11,245-byte multi-op graph and does not apply to the single-Conv reality. Empirical confirmation: `nobias` (0/265, ch0 lights diamond cells), `nobias_redesign` a₀=7>0 (0/265, lights padding col c=W rows 6–10), `a0zero` a₀=0 (0/265, lights row5 foreground c0,c2,c4,c6). Bidirectional contradiction on `a₀`.

## Don't-do log

- **[2026-07-03 batch48] Do NOT try to drop/shrink the Conv bias.** The 10-element bias is forced (floor proof above): row-5 odd carve forces `a₀>0`, padding cell output(10,W) forces `a₀≤0`. No bias-free single Conv exists. Verified on the official grader (`verify_subset` semantics), not just ng_gate (whose local `decode(arr,h,w)` ignores padding and would *falsely* pass an unclean-padding candidate — GRADER-GAP).
